conceptZh: 扭蛋小怪獸從冷冷的冰箱扭蛋裡蹦出來，兩邊拉扯冰條，筆畫「啪」地彈回原位。
object: a fuzzy round gachapon pocket creature with a toy fridge
morph: two teams of icicle-shaped strokes are tugged apart by the creature and a frosty fridge door, then spring together into 冷
creativeAngle: 以冰箱門和小怪獸拔河，冷氣把小怪獸吹得抖成毛球。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a pale butter-yellow background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 冷 as the only text on screen, drawn in icy cobalt blue solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a mint-green gachapon capsule pops open and a round fuzzy lavender creature with big eyes bursts out and ricochets off the frame edges, landing in front of a small toy fridge as the first 冷 is spoken and the two stroke groups (the two-dot ice part on the left, the 令 part on the right) float in from opposite sides. 1.7-3.5s: the creature grabs the left ice-dot piece in its mouth while the fridge door swings open and sucks the right piece the other way, a comic tug-of-war with the creature's fur stretching like taffy, the second 冷 spoken as the pieces SPRING together into the glyph with a rubbery boing. 3.5-5s: a gust of cold air whooshes from the open fridge and blows the creature backward into a spinning fluff-ball with frosty shivering, the word 冷氣 spoken as a little cartoon blue air-conditioner-style breeze swirls out of the fridge (animated swirl only, no text). The creature then shakes off and gives a double-take at the glyph. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "冷、冷、冷氣" (ㄌㄥˇ、ㄌㄥˇ、ㄌㄥˇ ㄑㄧˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 冷 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 積木小隊和調皮小老鼠拔河搶一條結霜的冰藍積木長鏈，拉到腳打滑、臉通紅，鏈子「啪」一聲斷開，兩邊都摔個屁股蹲，彈飛的冰藍積木落下疊成「冷」，斷口還噴出一道冷水把大家澆得直發抖。
object: a long frosted ice-blue chain of interlocking bricks, tugged between the brick squad and the cheeky mouse
morph: the chain snaps; two short frosted segments drop on the left as the 冫 ice dots, and the longer segments spring upward and stack on the right into the 令 part, completing 冷
creativeAngle: 和前一版的扭蛋怪獸、冰箱吸力完全不同：這次用指定的積木小隊當主角，拔河的對象是一條會結霜的冰藍積木鏈，斷掉時鏈段本身彈成筆畫，主角與老鼠留在兩側不碰字。詞改用「冷水」，斷口噴水讓聲音和畫面同步，而且中途「頂上積木掉下來」是看得見的失誤，結尾的抖抖與頭頂一碰則是收尾小笑點。
promptEn:
An 8-second 2D cartoon clip on a pale butter-yellow background, warm bright palette, nothing behind the action. The only text ever on screen is one Traditional Chinese glyph 冷, drawn in saturated solid cobalt-blue strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins.

The lead is a brick squad: five chunky red and orange interlocking toy bricks stacked into a stubby little figure with a painted determined face and tiny clip-on feet, who marches with a proud bossy strut. The rival is an original tiny cartoon mouse with huge round ears, grey, lightning fast, always grinning.

0-1.5s: A long frosted ice-blue chain of clicked-together bricks lies across the floor, steaming with cold mist. The brick squad stomps in from the left and clamps the left end, pointing at it with a possessive grunt. The mouse zips in from the right in a blur, grabs the other end and winks. The voice says the first 冷 as both grip the chain.

1.5-3.5s: Tug-of-war. The squad leans back so far its feet skid in little squiggles; the mouse digs in its heels, tail stiff. Both faces turn tomato red. The frosty chain stretches like taffy, frost cracking off it. The squad heaves too hard and its top brick pops off its head and bounces away, so it wobbles and grabs the chain again one brick shorter, grinning sheepishly.

3.5-5s: A frozen beat, everything trembling, then the chain SNAPS in the middle with a rubbery twang. Squad and mouse fly backwards and land on their bottoms at opposite frame edges, dizzy with spinning stars. The flung ice-blue segments spring into the center: two short pieces drop on the left as the two 冫 ice dots, and the longer pieces stack and click on the right into 令, completing a perfectly formed 冷. The voice says the second 冷 as the last piece clicks home.

5-8s: The glyph 冷 holds perfectly still and fully readable for the final 3 seconds. Off to the side, the broken chain end spurts a cartoon fountain of cold blue water that sprinkles the squad and the mouse; the voice says 冷水 exactly as the water sprays. Both shiver happily with chattering teeth, hug themselves, then the squad's lost top brick drops back onto its head with a small bonk and it strikes a proud pose, never touching the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly these syllables, slowly and distinctly with clear tones: 冷、冷、冷水 (ㄌㄥˇ、ㄌㄥˇ、ㄌㄥˇ ㄕㄨㄟˇ), a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word. No other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, only soft sound effects and quiet music under the voice. No watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
